test_title: PYST 54: SSC MTS 2024 - English Language and Comprehension (Held On: 11 Nov, 2024 - Shift 1)
subject: english
question: Select the option that has used the correct tense.

options.text: He realised he had forgotten his keys after he had leave the house.
He realised he had forgotten his keys after he had left the house.
He realised he had forgotten his keys after he has leave the house.
He realised he had forgotten his keys after he was left the house.

solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. He realised he had forgotten his keys after he had left the house .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence involves the use of the **past perfect tense** to indicate the sequence of events in the past.
 
• In the sentence, the action of "leaving the house" occurred **before** the action of "realising" and "forgetting the keys."
 
• The correct construction uses the **past perfect tense** for the earlier action (had left the house) and the **simple past tense** for the later action (realised).

Correct sentence: *He realised he had forgotten his keys after he had left the house*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Explanation of incorrect options:**
 
 
• **Option 1:** "had leave" is grammatically incorrect. The correct past participle of "leave" is "left."
 
• **Option 3:** "has leave" is incorrect because "has" is present perfect and does not fit the context of the past sequence of events.
 
• **Option 4:** "was left" suggests a passive voice, which changes the meaning of the sentence and is incorrect in this context.
 
 
 
• **Usage of past perfect:**
 
 
• Past perfect is used to indicate the earlier of two past actions in a sentence.
 
• Example: By the time I arrived, they **had left**.
